articles.title: Ferrari facing 'very challenging times' - Hamilton
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari are facing "very, very challenging times" as a result of the series of on-track incidents between himself and team-mate Charles Leclerc.
body: The two drivers had talks on Thursday after arriving at the Qatar Grand Prix to discuss the fall-out from their collision in the race in Las Vegas last weekend, which team boss Frederic Vasseur said was "completely unacceptable".
Both said the conclusion of those discussions would "stay internal" but admitted a solution needed to be found.
Hamilton said: "I like to think that we're stronger from these difficult...
"If everything was just great all the time, I don't think you learn anything when you're winning all the time. You learn really through the hardest times.

articles.title: GB win decider to reach Davis Cup semis for first time since 2019
articles.summary: Great Britain advance to the semi-finals of the Davis Cup for the first time since 2019 as Henry Patten and Neal Skupski win a decisive doubles tie against Germany in Bologna.
body: Great Britain advanced to the semi-finals of the Davis Cup for the first time since 2019 as Henry Patten and Neal Skupski won a decisive doubles tie against third seeds Germany in Bologna.
Patten and Skupski, playing together for the first time since announcing their doubles partnership for the 2027 season, proved too clinical for Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz.
They converted two break points and saved five in the first set, before overturning a mini-break in the tie-break to win 6-2 7-6 (8-6).

Skupski was involved in a Davis Cup quarter-final loss playing alongside Joe Salisbury against the same German doubles pair in December 2021 - a defeat that was in his mind as Thursday's decider progressed.

articles.title: SFA to deliver revised proposal after young player vote delayed
articles.summary: The Scottish FA will continue consulting with SPFL clubs in a bid to get more game time for homegrown talent after initial plans put forward by the governing body failed to reach a member vote.
body: Following an all-club meeting at St Andrews in September, the SFA proposed financial incentives - and penalties - along with quotas, in a bid to get more youngsters playing for clubs.
Initially, these proposals were to have been voted on at a SFA general meeting in October and the SPFL's annual meeting this month.
But the SFA now say they are aiming to put refreshed proposals to the clubs in the first quarter of 2027, in time for the start of the 2027-28 season.

Despite the governing body saying they are "encouraged", they add that "recent discussions have spawned a range of additional potential innovations that all parties agree will require further consultation."

articles.title: Fofana has apologised for interview - Alonso
articles.summary: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso says defender Wesley Fofana has apologised for his controversial comments in an interview he gave without permission from the club.
body: Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso says defender Wesley Fofana has apologised for a controversial interview he gave on YouTube.
Fofana has been criticised for comments he made in the interview with YouTuber Zach Nani in which he appeared to joke about his penalty miss in a Carabao Cup shootout defeat at Liverpool.
He did not have permission to hold the two-hour interview, which was aired after Chelsea 's humiliating 4-1 defeat at home to rivals Leeds on Saturday, but Alonso said the matter was now "closed".

"It was unfortunate. He has apologised. He knows it was not right, the moment, it was not right, the content," said the Blues boss, who was speaking before Friday's Premier League match at Nottingham Forest.

articles.title: Russell: I found Verstappen comments amusing
articles.summary: George Russell says he was "amused" by Max Verstappen’s criticism of him after their feud reignited at the Las Vegas Grand Prix but admits it was "avoidable".
body: After colliding on track in final practice last weekend, Russell publicly criticised Verstappen following the incident. The Dutchman won the race after an intense battle between them and said afterwards that the Mercedes driver is "far below my level".

The pair have clashed several times on track in the past, most notably engaging in a remarkable war of words following an incident during qualifying at the 2024 Qatar Grand Prix where Verstappen felt Russell had pushed unreasonably hard for him to be penalised.

Speaking on Thursday - back at the Lusail International Circuit almost exactly two years on from that incident - ahead of this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix, Russell said: "At the end of the day, I guess I stand by what I said after practice.

"But he was the one who went out and won the race. I didn't and I'm sure he had a bit of a laugh about that, and that was reasonably amusing. From my side, just a new race weekend, try and focus on the driving and move on."

articles.title: DP World Tour player vows to 'kick butt' in battle with brain tumour
articles.summary: DP World Tour player MJ Daffue has vowed to ‘kick butt and be ready to go soon’, having been forced to miss the start of the season after being diagnosed with a brain tumour.
body: Daffue won twice on the HotelPlanner Tour this season and finished fifth in the Road to Mallorca rankings, securing his DP World Tour card, before being hospitalised earlier this month for an infection that unearthed further health issues.
The 37-year-old has since revealed two tumours were found, including one benign on the liver, with Daffue now undergoing treatment to address the one found in his brain.

In a statement on his Instagram, Daffue said: "It's taken a while to post anything about this year because of the difficult time the past two weeks has been. This year has been incredible and we have been so blessed with good golf.
"Unfortunately, I ended up in the hospital with an infection about 10 days ago and after lots of tests they could not find the source. However they did find a tumour on my brain and my liver.

articles.title: 'You can't sit still and do nothing!' - MVG 'buzzing' for world title bid
articles.summary: Michael van Gerwen is ready to take a pre-tournament scouting mission to Alexandra Palace ahead of his bid for a fourth World Darts Championship title next month, live on Sky Sports.
body: The Dutchman produced an impressive run to the Grand Slam of Darts semi-finals earlier this month, where he fired a nine-darter in the first leg of his quarter-final victory over Tom Sykes before being knocked out by compatriot Gian van Veen.

Van Gerwen is keen to build on his Wolverhampton performance at this weekend's Players Championship Finals ahead of turning attention to the Worlds, where he will be among the favourites to lift the Sid Waddell Trophy.
"That [consistency] is what you also need, especially at this time of year - you want to do yourself favours," Van Gerwen told Sky Sports. "We all know I had a tough period but you need to move on.

"You can't sit still and do nothing - you have to practise, you have to put time and effort in to produce some good darts. The field is wide, there's so many good players now, so you have to move along.

articles.title: Stephen A. Smith urges Steelers’ owner to make major firing alongside Mike McCarthy
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers were battling for the top spot of the AFC North just two weeks ago; now they find themselves embroiled in a complete PR disaster. Aaron Rodgers’ public outburst over Mike McCarthy has taken over the NFL over the last 24 hours.
body: McCarthy is certainly coming under scrutiny for some of the accusations made by Rodgers, but Steelers fan Stephen A. Smith has admitted he wants to see someone else inside the building in Pittsburgh fired by the owner alongside the head coach.

It is hard to see how McCarthy can continue as the head coach after a number of the Steelers’ players anonymously confirmed Rodgers’ claims. There was one claim involving general manager Omar Khan that Smith was disgusted with.

“Omar Khan, this GM that I am no fan of in terms of the job that he has done: I don’t know him personally, but he ain’t done a great job, okay? It’s just a fact, all right? He took over in 2022, and still can’t find a quarterback,” Smith said on First Take.

“So to me, when I hear Aaron Rodgers say that the GM and him were in the hallway and they were joking about what they saw from Mike McCarthy, if I’m the owner of the Steelers, guess what, Evan? Guess what, Hawk? They gone. They gone today. I got a problem with them coaching this Friday.

articles.title: Steelers President Art Rooney expresses full confidence in Mike McCarthy
articles.summary: Wednesday was one of the wildest days in the history of the Pittsburgh Steelers. After benching Aaron Rodgers late Tuesday night, the four-time MVP went on The Pat McAfee Show and aired out a lot of grievances largely pertaining to head coach Mike McCarthy.
body: Among the issues Rodgers put on blast were McCarthy routinely falling asleep in meetings, being late for walkthroughs and meetings, not knowing the gameplay, and breaking down a team huddle vs. the Eagles by saying, “1-2-3 Packers.”

Several insiders have noted that players have backed up these claims made by Rodgers, which led many to believe McCarthy’s days in Pittsburgh could and should be numbered. However, Team President Art Rooney II expressed faith in the Steelers’ head coach.

“I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney said via Gerry Dulac. “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.”
The Steeles will face the Broncos on Black Friday in their first home game since they defeated the Cleveland Browns 27-6 to secure a 6-2 record. Oh how much has changed since then.

articles.title: ‘She’s fearless’: Fox News continues with bizarre Sophie Cunningham coverage
articles.summary: Fox News has been relentless in its coverage of WNBA guard Sophie Cunningham this month. The network has had a fixation on Cunningham since she told ESPN in July that she wanted to protect young girls from competing against “biological men,” and in the days after Republicans lost control of both…
body: The network ran multiple segments on her, with political journalist Aaron Rupar calling the coverage “beyond parody.”

Last week, Cunningham gave the network even more content to work with after appearing on the cover of Maxim ‘s November/December issue and describing what she is looking for in a partner in her interview with the magazine.

“I have a very high standard for my future husband. He’ll be someone who is Christ-centered and can lead me in my walk with Jesus. Someone who’s friendly, confident, and secure. Someone who is taller than me and athletic and just a good human with similar morals and values,” Cunningham told Maxim.

With photos from the cover shoot playing in the background, Fox’s panel praised her Christian faith and went through her list of what she wants in a husband. Fox & Friends co-host Ainsley Earhardt then told single Christian men watching at home to “blow up her DM,” and plenty of people online could not believe what they were seeing.

articles.title: What all 32 NFL teams should be thankful for this Thanksgiving
articles.summary: From MVP candidates Joe Burrow and Brock Purdy to promising rookies, new coaches and future draft picks, here is one reason each of the NFL's 32 teams can give thanks
body: On an electric NFL Thanksgiving, I brought together my fellow CBS Sports writers Bryan DeArdo, Jordan Dajani, Carter Bahns and Garrett Podell to find one thing each team can be thankful for this holiday season.

Thanksgiving offers a natural opportunity to take stock of the good things, even during an NFL season that has not gone according to plan for every team. Some franchises enter the holiday firmly in the Super Bowl race, while others are already measuring progress through young players, improved units and the draft capital that could shape a brighter future.

Winning despite turnovers – The Bills have a lot of reasons for gratitude. This one is somewhat of a good news, bad news situation: the team is turning the ball over more than they should, but they are still getting wins. It just goes to show that great teams will find ways to win games regardless. Josh Allen, James Cook, and their record are the obvious things they should be thankful for, but this one is most interesting to me because, as a team that has turned the ball over twice in three of the last four games and five times in a single game this season, 9-1 is impressive.
